overall: Atlanta is off to a hot start this Independence Day, with temperatures already at 82.4°F by 9:50 AM ET and warming at a brisk +3.6°F/hr under mostly sunny skies and calm winds. Conditions are primed for a significant afternoon heat-up: high humidity (dewpoint 71.6°F), light wind, and only scattered clouds are offering minimal resistance to solar heating. The slight chance of afternoon convection (20% PoP) is unlikely to materially cap the high given its late timing.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread — GFS is the hottest at 98.3°F, HRRR at 95.5°F, ECMWF at 94.4°F, and NBM the coolest at 92.9°F — but the META model (most reliable) consolidates heavily into the 98-99°F bucket at 52.8% and 96-97°F at 33.7%, together accounting for 86.5% of probability mass. The NWS text forecast of 'high near 96°F' aligns with the lower end of this range, while the current warming trajectory from 82.4°F at ~10 AM with peak expected near 2:30 PM is consistent with an eventual high in the upper 90s.
max_temp_prediction: The dominant signal from the META model (52.8% on 98-99°F) combined with GFS at 98.3°F and a current warming pace that projects into the upper 90s by early-to-mid afternoon points to a likely high in the 97–99°F range. The active Kalshi market uses EVEN buckets; while the ensemble model's top even bucket is 96-97°F at 25.6%, the META model — which is considered most reliable — assigns 52.8% to the 98-99°F even bucket, making that the statistically favored outcome. Confidence is moderate-to-high given model convergence in the upper 90s, with the primary downside risk being an earlier-than-forecast convective event that truncates afternoon heating.
